newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland's Quinn welcomes Moody's rating upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Ireland's Quinn welcomes Moody's rating upgrade.

text.p: Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn on Thursday welcomed the announcement by Moody's Investors Service that it had upgraded the foreign currency long term debt rating assigned to the Irish government's debt.
The international credit rating upgraded the foreign-currency sovereign ceilings for bonds and bank deposits of Ireland Aa1 from Aa2.
At the same time, the rating agency confirmed its rating of Aaa on the government of Ireland's domestic-currency debt.

"This announcement represents a significant achievement for Ireland and should improve the attractiveness of Irish government securities for investors both at home and abroad," Quinn said in a statement.
"This upgrade is tangible confirmation by an independent observer of the very significant progress made by Ireland on fiscal and economic consolidation in recent years.
"The upgrade also reflects the positive outlook for the future of the Irish economy," he said.

Moody's said that its upgrade of the foreign-currency sovereign ceiling was based on the strong performance of Ireland's economy during the past several years and on Ireland's likely participation at an early stage in European Monetary Union (EMU).
